vl_cyclist.text: It's a national cycle route now, where the trains used to be. National Route 51. Bletchley to Oxford one way and Cambridge the other.
You can still see where the platforms were. And the signal boxes. And the pie shops that have not noticed.

vl_volunteer.text: The R101 was the biggest flying thing in the world. It was nearly as long as the Titanic. It carried fifty-odd people out over France in bad weather, and that was the last we ever knew of her.
We were so proud of her. Then, in a field near Beauvais, we had a funeral.

vl_pilgrim.text: They locked Bunyan up for preaching. He was in Bedford gaol twelve years, off and on. He made shoelaces to support his family and wrote in between.
Pilgrim's Progress. Christian, a heavy pack, a long road. You can see why he'd be a Varsity Line man.

vl_codebreaker.text: My nan worked at Bletchley Park. She never told us what she did, not till she was eighty. Then she said: 'I broke a very big code'. And went to put the kettle on.
There were about ten thousand people there at the peak, and three out of four were women.
